name: Pure Instruction Alignment
hypothesis: Fine-tuning exclusively on curated instruction pairs maximizes task adherence and format following, but carries a high risk of catastrophic forgetting of base pretraining representations.
expected_benefits: Rapid learning of User/Assistant turn boundaries and high compliance on direct questions.
failure_risks: Substantial degradation of Stage C general language modeling loss (+0.50 or higher).

name: Balanced Alignment with Foundational Replay
hypothesis: Combining 80% instruction tuning with 20% Stage C pretraining replay provides optimal instruction alignment while strictly preserving base multilingual and coding representations.
loss_masking: hybrid (assistant_only for SFT, full_causal for replay)
expected_benefits: High instruction compliance with minimal foundational drift (Stage C validation loss drift < +0.20).
failure_risks: Slightly slower convergence on formatting constraints compared to pure SFT.

name: Multilingual-Prioritized Alignment
hypothesis: Equalizing instruction data weight across English, Hindi Devanagari, and Hinglish prevents English from dominating vocabulary predictions and prevents Devanagari subword collapse.
expected_benefits: Symmetric multilingual instruction following without degradation in Devanagari generation.
failure_risks: Lower peak performance on English technical explanations.

name: Multi-Turn Context & Reasoning Specialization
hypothesis: Training with structured multi-turn dialogue histories (2-3 turns) and step-by-step arithmetic/logic chains will establish context retention and entity consistency across conversation turns.
expected_benefits: Strong context retention on pronoun resolution, entity binding, and multi-turn state tracking.
failure_risks: Risk of length truncation as multi-turn sequences approach the 512-token limit.
